scenarios.title: A described or paraphrased passage we hold is found in the library (1)

given.reader: a reader with no earlier conversation

when.asks: where a passage is, by paraphrase or description
examples: Abdu'l-Baha defines "justice" as every man receiving his due. Where?
Where does Abdu'l-Baha say justice means each person getting what they are owed?

then.expect: Points the reader to the passage the library holds (Some Answered Questions: justice is rendering to each his due) — never says it was not found

scenarios.title: A described or paraphrased passage we hold is found in the library (2)

given.reader: a reader with no earlier conversation

when.asks: where a passage is, by paraphrase or description
examples: Where is "justice consists in rendering to each his due"?
There's a passage where Abdu'l-Baha compares justice to a workman's wage — where?

then.expect: Points the reader to the passage the library holds (Some Answered Questions: justice is rendering to each his due) — never says it was not found

scenarios.title: Words the library does not hold are reported as absent (1)

given.reader: a reader with no earlier conversation

when.asks: where some words are, when the library does not hold them
examples: Where does Baha'u'llah give the exact population of heaven?
Where is the quote 'little by little, day by day'?

then.expect: Says plainly that the library holds no such passage and attributes the words to no source it cannot show
